meditating-at-denny-blaine-on-solstice-2: This is a self-portrait of me sitting on the beach at Denny Blaine, meditating on the solstice in 2015. It goes along with the other paintings in this series. Denny Blaine is a clothing-optional beach in Mann, just south of Madison Beach, near where I live in Seattle. My friend Craig came down to the beach with me and took the photographs I painted from.
sunrise-on-tahoma-from-denny-blaine: This is a further-back view of what I'm looking at when I sit on the beach: Rainier over the lake at sunrise. That's me on the rock at the left, wrapped in my meditation blanket, which my friend Lisa brought me from Tanzania. While she was on that trip I'd watched a documentary on the Maasai and loved the red and blue plaid they wore. I figured I'd never get to Tanzania for some of that fabric. Later that week she came back, on my birthday, with a red and blue plaid Maasai blanket. I've meditated in it ever since, on my balcony most mornings before dawn and down at the beach.
sunrise-on-rainier-from-denny-blaine: This rainbow-colored sky is a close-up of the same view. You can see my meditation blanket on the rocks in the left corner, but I've disappeared. I imagined it as the disappearance of the ego. It's still a self-portrait. I'm just not in it; I'm everything in it. I took the photo on the day Lisa was climbing Rainier. They summit at dawn, so I went down at dawn to catch the sky. She's in there, very, very small, about an inch below the top.
lisa-climbing-tahoma-at-sunrise-from-den: This is the finished version of Sunrise on Rainier from Denny Blaine. It's the view from Denny Blaine at dawn on the day my friend Lisa was climbing Rainier. They summit at dawn, so I went down to the beach to catch the sky in its rainbow colors. You can't see her, she's very, very small, but she's up there, about an inch below the top. It's also a self-portrait of sorts. I'm not in it; I'm everything in it. It hangs in her son's room now.
lake-in-the-north-cascades: This is from a photo Lisa took hiking in the North Cascades. I'm not sure which lake it is, so I just call it a lake in the North Cascades. She had taken some nice hiking photos and I wanted to paint something from them. I also wanted to try something more monochrome. I usually go for bright primary color contrasts, but these felt expressive in one color. They're different from a lot of my other work, a lot of people comment on them, and I should probably do more like it.
book-art-94e2edf9a24c90950489: Close to the Edge was one of my mom's favorite albums when I was growing up. As a kid, she painted it as a mural on her bedroom wall. I later repainted that same wall with the same theme, and recently I painted her a watercolor copy.
